claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy microstructure consists of dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
Introducing a high fraction of coincidence site lattice boundaries will improve strength relative to an unmodified lamellar-colony microstructure.
Introducing a high fraction of coincidence site lattice boundaries will improve room-temperature tensile ductility relative to an unmodified lamellar-colony microstructure.
Coincidence site lattice boundaries have lower interfacial energy than the boundaries they replace.
Coincidence site lattice boundaries have higher resistance to microcracking than the boundaries they replace.
Coincidence site lattice boundaries reduce microcrack initiation during room-temperature tensile deformation.
Coincidence site lattice boundaries reduce microcrack propagation during room-temperature tensile deformation.
Reduced microcrack initiation and propagation increases room-temperature tensile ductility.
Retention of a fine grain size maintains tensile strength after grain-boundary engineering.
The proposed beneficial regime is a grain size of 1–5 μm.
The proposed beneficial regime is a coincidence site lattice boundary fraction of 0.5–0.8.
The proposed beneficial regime requires coincidence site lattice boundaries to be randomly distributed throughout the material.
